event: Wren spends three days writing her reply to Sorrel.
She keeps out what is not hers to include: the dual signal, the corruption's shallowness, Brecca's insight.
She writes the intervals plainly: 18, 36, 55, Pulse 4 at Day 75 if the rate holds.
She asks Sorrel to bring interval records and to come when convenient, for two weeks.
She seals it and gives it to Hadley for the next supply cache run.
Hadley sets off with the letter.
With the pulse twenty days off, she has her longest clear interval since arriving.
She surveys the retreated strip every other morning; the gap is six degrees by Day 58.
Each degree exposes about three meters of limestone, pale and smelling of water and calcite.
The corruption rinses out: first the chemistry, then the texture, finally the substrate signal.
On Day 60 [Keen Survey] returns a clean trace of dressed limestone heading east-northwest.
Three channels or three branches of one system: not water table, construction.
She maps what the survey gives her and marks the gaps clearly.
On Day 61 Theron clears the T-junction's eastern branch.
Two meters in, he swaps trowel for hands: the next surface is what he has been looking for.
Wren watches from the channel margin.
At the end of the morning the terminal structure's first block emerges.
It is lighter, denser limestone set at a different angle: a meeting point.
Its face holds a precise circular recess about eight centimeters across: a mark.
'It is the same geometry as the carved depression on the threshold stone's west face.'
She looks twenty meters to the stone; she once took that depression for weathering.
'Write it down.' He already has his notebook out.
The gap reaches seven degrees by Day 63.
Day 64: at the retreated strip with Detail Notation, the Eye's transmission sharpens.
For about four seconds she senses its depth: below the construction layer.
Then the resolution drops back and the clarity is gone.
She stands between the terminal block, the Eye to the north and the unreleased south.
She journals: the relay terminus is below builder level, possibly pre-corruption.
Day 68: Hadley returns from the cache run with three species he cannot identify.
The small dark limestone-walkers are back: eleven on two square meters of new stone.
They gather at the active boundary and thin once it moves on.
'The substrate signal clearing,' Wren says. 'Can you test that?'
With [Keen Survey] and Detail Notation she reads mid-range signal: stone recovering its frequency.
'I can't tell you what they're eating. But they're on the recovery frequency.'
Hadley writes it down, keeping observation and explanation apart.
On the morning of Day 69 Sorrel walks in behind Hadley.
Wren expected someone older; Sorrel is about her age, with a careful stillness.
Sorrel looks at the threshold stone before looking at anyone.
'You're Wren.' 'And you're Sorrel.'
Sorrel stands at the east face without touching it, studying the carved depression.
'How long has this been here?' 'Since before the settlement. The stone itself is older.'
Sorrel reads the site with full attention and no expression.
'Where is the corruption boundary?' 'I'll show you after breakfast.'
Sorrel eats standing at the fire pit, reading the gap.
Three questions: Detail Notation's reach, how signal degrades, the Vael's depth.
From the escarpment the pulse is a frequency shift, not a wave front, but the timing matches.
Sorrel's interval notebook begins at Day 18 and matches Wren's count.
The original cycle was seventeen days; deceleration began before either arrived.
'Your grief hypothesis. I've been watching something that makes me uncertain.' 'Tell me.'
Wren tells it all in the order it happened: dual signal, the Vael, the four-second window.
Sorrel asks whether the Vael is prior to the corruption; Wren cannot yet tell.
'If it's prior, the corruption isn't responding to absence. It's responding to presence.'
Wren: then the pulse slows because the presence it responds to is changing.
Sorrel: or the corruption responds to something it doesn't understand, and the cycle is its adjustment rate.
For the first time since Day 39, Wren is not approaching it alone.
An observation cross-validates both counts and updates Sorrel's hypothesis: +55 XP.

changes.note: Observation: Sorrel cross-site data validation and synthesis

event: Sorrel spends the afternoon at the channel with Theron, sketching the terminal block.
That evening Wren sits at the threshold stone, palm on the east face, the Vael beneath.
The precursor's compression sits above it; the Vael runs through both unchanged.
Sorrel writes by firelight three meters away; the circular depression drew their recognition.
Wren does not ask yet; there will be time.
The pulse is six days off, as is the marks' expiry; she holds it all as one field.
She journals: Sorrel arrived; the corruption is not responding to absence.
The ghost-elms' shimmer carries further south than the morning she arrived.
